mission.title: Install and Configure Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP)
mission.description: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) is an enterprise Kubernetes distribution that provides a developer-friendly platform for building, deploying, and managing containerized applications. It includes additional features such as a web console, integrated CI/CD, and enhanced security. Key trade-offs include the complexity of setup and management compared to vanilla Kubernetes, and licensing costs for enterprise support.

steps.title: Install the OpenShift CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the OpenShift command-line interface (CLI) which is essential for interacting with the OpenShift cluster.

```bash

curl -LO https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/openshift-client-linux-4.17.0.tar.gz

tar -xvf openshift-client-linux-4.17.0.tar.gz

sudo mv oc kubectl /usr/local/bin/

```

> Download the OpenShift CLI for version 4.17.0.
> Extract the downloaded tarball.
> Move the binaries to a directory in your PATH.

steps.title: Create an OpenShift cluster
steps.description:
This command creates a new OpenShift cluster with the specified version and node count in a given region.

```bash

openshift-install create cluster --dir=cluster --log-level=info

```

> Replace 'cluster' with your desired directory name.

steps.title: Configure kubeconfig
steps.description:
This step sets up the kubeconfig file to allow kubectl and oc commands to interact with the new OpenShift cluster.

```bash

export KUBECONFIG=$(pwd)/cluster/auth/kubeconfig

```

> Set the KUBECONFIG environment variable to point to the kubeconfig file.

steps.title: Verify cluster nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in the OpenShift cluster to ensure they are running correctly.

```bash

oc get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes listed with a status of 'Ready'.

steps.title: Post-install configuration
steps.description:
This step configures autoscaling and monitoring for your OpenShift cluster.

```bash

oc apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/cluster-autoscaler/master/deploy/cluster-autoscaler-operator.yaml

oc apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openshift/cluster-monitoring-operator/master/deploy/cluster-monitoring-operator.yaml

```

> Deploy the Cluster Autoscaler.
> Deploy the Monitoring Operator.

uninstall.title: Remove the OpenShift cluster
uninstall.description:
This command will delete the OpenShift cluster and all associated resources, which may result in data loss.

```bash

openshift-install destroy cluster --dir=cluster --log-level=info

```

> Replace 'cluster' with your cluster directory.

uninstall.title: Clean up orphaned resources
uninstall.description:
This command will help to clean up any orphaned resources that may remain after cluster deletion.

```bash

kubectl delete pvc --all

kubectl delete services --all

```

> Delete all persistent volume claims.
> Delete all services.

upgrade.title: Upgrade the OpenShift cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your cluster and check for any deprecated APIs. This step performs the upgrade and verifies the cluster status post-upgrade.

```bash

oc adm upgrade --to-image=<new-version-image>

oc get nodes

oc get clusterversion

```

> Replace <new-version-image> with the image of the new version.
> Verify that all nodes are in 'Ready' state after the upgrade.
> Check the cluster version to confirm the upgrade was successful.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp <ip>:<port>: connect: connection refused'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The OpenShift API server is not running or is unreachable.

**Fix:**
Check the status of the API server pods using 'oc get pods -n openshift-apiserver'.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient CPU resources available'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The cluster does not have enough CPU resources to schedule new pods.

**Fix:**
Scale up your cluster by adding more nodes or increasing the size of existing nodes.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'ImagePullBackOff'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** The specified container image cannot be pulled from the registry.

**Fix:**
Verify the image name and ensure the image is available in the specified registry.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'NodeNotReady'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** One or more nodes are not in a ready state due to various issues.

**Fix:**
Check the node status with 'oc describe node <node-name>' for more details.

versionNotes.changes: Introduced support for Kubernetes 1.30, enhanced security features, and improved monitoring capabilities.
versionNotes.deprecations: Deprecated certain legacy APIs and features related to networking.
versionNotes.migrationSteps: Review the deprecated features and update your configurations accordingly.

resolution.summary: You should see output from 'oc get nodes' showing all nodes in 'Ready' state, confirming that the OpenShift cluster is operational.
